It is pretty much meaningless. Most polls mean very little. This poll I would argue is even more meaningless then most polls. It is asking an opinion of the individuals "favorite potential Democratic candidate" while only offering two options. Secondly, it is asking anyone, when usually for an accurate sample your subject would be "likely voters", "registered voters", or something similar.

Polls like this are designed to elicit a response to the result and are not meant to be used as a source of reference.

IMO this poll does have some value even if it's internet based.

First the sample size is HUGE - over three quarters of a million! Compare that to traditional telephone polls where the sample is 1000-2000 (source: I worked for one of the most frequently cited US polling institutes).

Second, traditional polls are carried out by calling thousands upon thousands of landlines to gather the sample. Problem is over 40% of US households have no landline. So you can guess my point that traditional polls are also imperfectly representative.

The next thing to do is compare previous Isidewith.com polls with the respective results and then decide how reliable it is.

Polling organizations do not only call land lines these days, they also call mobiles. That's been the norm for at least the last five years. No one would hire a polling company that ignored mobiles.

The sample size doesn't matter because it has a sampling bias built into it. Unless it's in the millions and the sampling bias mirrors who votes it isn't statistically valid.
